title: Solomon's Succession and the Securing of the Throne

date.label: Undated 1 Kings narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: David is old and stricken in years; clothes cannot warm him. His servants bring Abishag the Shunammite to cherish and minister to him, "but the king knew her not."
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: Adonijah son of Haggith exalts himself — "I will be king" — with chariots, horsemen, and fifty men to run before him. He confers with Joab son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest, who follow him.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: David had not displeased Adonijah at any time in saying, "Why hast thou done so?" Adonijah was a very goodly man, and his mother bare him after Absalom.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and the mighty men which belonged to David are not with Adonijah. Adonijah sacrifices by the stone of Zoheleth at En-rogel and calls all the king's sons and the men of Judah — but not Nathan, Benaiah, the mighty men, or Solomon.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: Nathan warns Bathsheba that Adonijah reigns and David does not know it, and counsels her to remind David of his oath that Solomon shall reign, promising to come in after her and confirm her words.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Nathan," read in full.

claims.claim: Bathsheba and Nathan tell David he swore that Solomon shall reign after him and sit upon his throne, and David then swears it in the scene. No record of such an oath exists in 2 Samuel; the oath is asserted in this scene, not established as predating it.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Bathsheba," read in full: "The earlier oath that Bathsheba mentions is not recorded anywhere else in Samuel or Kings."

claims.claim: Bathsheba goes in to the very old king (Abishag ministering), rehearses the oath, reports Adonijah's feast and the men he called, and warns that when David sleeps with his fathers she and Solomon shall be counted offenders.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Bathsheba," read in full.

claims.claim: Nathan enters while Bathsheba still speaks, bows before the king, and asks whether David himself has said Adonijah shall reign — "thou hast not shewed it unto thy servant" — reporting the feast and the men Adonijah did not call.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Nathan," read in full.

claims.claim: David swears by the LORD that even as he swore, "Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne in my stead; even so will I certainly do this day." Bathsheba bows and says, "Let my lord king David live for ever."
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: David orders Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to set Solomon on his own mule, bring him down to Gihon, and anoint him king over Israel with trumpet and acclamation, "God save king Solomon." Zadok takes a horn of oil out of the tabernacle and anoints Solomon; the people pipe and rejoice "so that the earth rent with the sound of them."
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Anointing," read in full (lines 0–151): Zadok took the horn of oil from the sacred tent and anointed Solomon at Gihon.

claims.claim: Adonijah and his guests hear the trumpet and the rejoicing as they finish eating; Jonathan son of Abiathar brings the news that David has made Solomon king, anointed at Gihon, sitting on the throne. All the guests are afraid, rise up, and go every man his way.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: Adonijah flees and catches hold on the horns of the altar. Solomon spares him conditionally — "If he will shew himself a worthy man, there shall not an hair of him fall to the earth: but if wickedness shall be found in him, he shall die" — brings him down from the altar, and sends him to his house.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: David charges Solomon to keep the charge of the LORD, walk in his ways, and keep the law of Moses, "that the LORD may continue his word… If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee a man on the throne of Israel."
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: The charge states the dynasty conditionally ("If thy children take heed"), while Nathan's oracle states it without condition ("And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever"). The two stand in tension, and the narrative does not resolve whether the condition qualifies the promise or the promise grounds the condition.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Nathan," read in full (the 2 Sam 7 oracle and its wording).

claims.claim: David recalls what Joab did to the two captains of the hosts of Israel, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, shedding their blood in peacetime as if in battle, and tells Solomon to act according to his wisdom and not let Joab's hoar head go down to the grave in peace.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Joab," read in full.

claims.claim: David charges Solomon to show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite and let them eat at his table, because they came to him when he fled because of Absalom.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: David names Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite of Bahurim, who cursed him with a grievous curse in the day he went to Mahanaim, and tells Solomon to hold him not guiltless but bring his hoar head down to the grave with blood.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: David sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David. He reigned forty years over Israel — seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem. Solomon sits upon the throne of David his father, and his kingdom is established greatly.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: Adonijah comes to Bathsheba and asks her to speak to Solomon that he give him Abishag the Shunammite to wife. He says the kingdom was his and all Israel set their faces on him to reign, but the kingdom is turned about and become his brother's. Bathsheba agrees to speak for him.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Bathsheba," read in full.

claims.claim: Solomon rises to meet his mother, bows to her, seats her at his right hand on a throne brought for the king's mother, and promises not to say her nay — but reads the request as a claim on the kingdom: "ask for him the kingdom also; for he is mine elder brother," naming Abiathar and Joab with him. Taking a former king's woman could signal a claim to his authority (compare 2 Sam 16:21–22).
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Bathsheba," read in full.

claims.claim: Solomon swears by the LORD in the self-imprecatory formula — "God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah have not spoken this word against his own life" — and sends Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who falls upon Adonijah so that he dies the same day. The formula is the same oath as Ruth 1:17, occurring twelve times in the Old Testament (Ruth once; Samuel and Kings eleven times).
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; reuse: `RCL-01-017` (probable, Ruth dossier), `SCL-01-027` (probable, 1 Samuel dossier), `S2CL-01-029` (probable, 2 Samuel S01 dossier).

claims.claim: Solomon sends Abiathar to his fields at Anathoth, sparing his life because he bore the ark of the Lord GOD before David his father and shared in all his father's affliction — the corrected KJV reading of 2:26 (the stored text misrenders the divine name; see §3) — and thrusts him out from being priest, "that he might fulfil the word of the LORD, which he spake concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh."
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "because thou didst bear the ark of the Lord GOD before David my father"); BiblicalTraining, "Shiloh," read in full (lines 0–148): the writer of Kings saw Abiathar's removal as the fulfilment of the word against Eli's house.

claims.claim: Tidings come to Joab, who had turned after Adonijah though not after Absalom; he flees to the tabernacle of the LORD and catches hold on the horns of the altar, refuses to come forth — "I will die here" — and Solomon commands Benaiah to fall upon him and bury him there, to take away the innocent blood which Joab shed. The law denies the altar's protection to one who kills deliberately (Ex 21:14).
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Joab," read in full.

claims.claim: Solomon declares that the LORD shall return Joab's blood upon his own head, for falling upon Abner and Amasa, "two men more righteous and better than he," without David's knowledge; their blood returns on Joab's head and his seed for ever, while upon David, his seed, his house, and his throne there shall be peace for ever from the LORD.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Joab," read in full.

claims.claim: Benaiah slays Joab, and Joab is buried in his own house in the wilderness. Solomon puts Benaiah in Joab's room over the host, and Zadok the priest in the room of Abiathar.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; BiblicalTraining, "Joab," read in full.

claims.claim: Solomon calls Shimei, orders him to build a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, and forbids him to go out or pass over the brook Kidron on pain of death — "thy blood shall be upon thine own head." Shimei agrees, and dwells in Jerusalem many days.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: At the end of three years two of Shimei's servants run away to Achish son of Maachah king of Gath; Shimei saddles his ass, goes to Gath to seek his servants, and brings them back from Gath.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: Solomon confronts Shimei for breaking the oath of the LORD and the king's commandment, recalls the wickedness Shimei did to David his father, and has Benaiah fall upon him so that he dies. "And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon."
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: The Cherethites and the Pelethites, David's royal guard, go down with Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah, set Solomon on David's mule, and bring him to Gihon; Jonathan's report names them again among those who went with Solomon.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; stored KJV read in full.

claims.claim: Solomon's succession is the first hereditary succession in Israel: hereditary kingship begins after David's death, when Solomon, though not his first-born son, succeeds him. Adonijah, the elder surviving son, claims the throne by birth order, and is passed over for the father's choice.
claims.evidence: Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre; Bible Odyssey, "Royal Succession," verified (registry) — not re-read in full in this dossier; cited only for the succession principles already quoted in the 2 Samuel S01 dossier.

connections.note: Nathan brings David the word that the LORD will build David a house: his offspring will succeed him and build a house for the LORD's name, and his throne will be established for ever. The promise is the ground on which Solomon's succession stands, and the charge in chapter 2 states it with a condition attached.

After the death of the first child, David comforts Bathsheba, and she bears Solomon; the text adds that the LORD loved the child, and through Nathan gives him the second name Jedidiah, loved by the LORD. The favour shown to the boy is the background of his succession.

God tells David that a son named Solomon will be born to him, a man of rest, who will build a house for the LORD's name. The Chronicler's account supplies the revelation behind the oath Bathsheba recalls, which no passage in Samuel or Kings records.

The men of Judah anoint David king over the house of Judah at Hebron. Solomon's anointing at Gihon follows the same rite — a king made by anointing — but it is performed by priest and prophet together, on the dying king's order.

On Ahithophel's counsel Absalom goes in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel, fulfilling Nathan's sentence. The act shows what taking a king's women meant in this world, and why Solomon reads Adonijah's request for Abishag as a claim on the kingdom.

An unnamed man of God tells Eli that his house will lose the priesthood: his sons will die, and a faithful priest will be raised up in its place. Solomon's removal of Abiathar is presented as the fulfilment of this word.

The law gives no protection to a man who kills another deliberately: even from the altar he is to be taken to die. The rule is the reason Joab's flight to the horns of the altar does not save him, where Adonijah's flight one chapter earlier did.

Shed blood defiles the land, and no atonement can be made for it except by the blood of the one who shed it. The principle stands behind Solomon's sentence that Joab's blood must return on his own head for the innocent blood of Abner and Amasa.

The law of the king provides for a future king chosen by the LORD, who must not multiply horses, wives, or silver and gold, and must keep a copy of the law and read it all his days. David's charge that Solomon keep the law of Moses is the charge in the law's own terms.

Joab lures Abner aside in the gate at Hebron to speak with him quietly and smites him, for the blood of Asahel his brother. David declares himself guiltless of Abner's blood and curses Joab's house, but keeps him as commander. The charge in chapter 2 recalls this killing as blood shed in peacetime.

Joab takes Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him, and smites him with his sword under the fifth rib. The second peacetime killing of a rival commander is the other innocent blood Solomon names when he orders Joab's death.

When David flees to Mahanaim, Barzillai the Gileadite brings beds, basins, wheat, barley, flour, parched corn, beans, lentils, honey, butter, sheep, and cheese for the king and his people. The kindness David repays to Barzillai's sons was shown to him in his flight.

Shimei son of Gera comes out of Bahurim as David flees, cursing him and throwing stones, calling him a bloody man. Abishai offers to take off his head, and David answers that the LORD may have bidden him curse. The curse is the wickedness Solomon recalls when Shimei breaks his confinement.

When David returns across the Jordan, Shimei falls before him, confesses, and begs not to be put to death, and David swears to him that he shall not die. The oath is the pardon Solomon inherits and qualifies with the confinement to Jerusalem.

Because Solomon's heart turns after other gods, the LORD says the kingdom will surely be rent from him and given to his servant, but not in his days and not wholly, for David's sake and for Jerusalem's sake. The sentence is the end toward which the conditional word of chapter 2 points.

All the tribes come to Hebron, recalling that David led Israel in war even under Saul, and the elders make a covenant with him and anoint him king over all Israel. The united throne David received here is the throne Solomon inherits, and the one Adonijah tried to take.
